articleBody:
- [ ] Measure the plumb and flatness of the bare wall studs using a 4-foot level — bowed framing causes uneven tile faces and noticeable lippage across large walls.
- [ ] Inspect existing drywall or plaster for moisture stains and mold — installing new tile over compromised surfaces guarantees eventual bond failure and rot.
- [ ] Confirm the build date of the property to verify EPA lead-safe renovation needs — homes built prior to 1978 require specific containment protocols before disturbing painted walls.
- [ ] Check the water absorption rating and manufacturer specifications for your chosen wall tile — porous ceramic tiles require different mortars than dense porcelain or natural marble slabs.
- [ ] Verify that you have purchased 10 to 15 percent extra tile over your square footage — cutting around plumbing valves, electrical outlets, and corners creates inevitable waste.
- [ ] Select color-matched 100 percent silicone sealant for all inside corners — grout placed in structural joints will crack as framing expands and contracts seasonally.
- [ ] Confirm proper backing material is on-site rather than standard drywall — wet bathroom zones demand cementitious backer units or water-resistant substrates.
- [ ] Review the cure schedule for your chosen setting mortar and grout — rushing the drying process can trap moisture and weaken the tile bond.

How to use this checklist

Walk through these verification points before demolition or setting begins. If your walls are severely out of plumb or show previous water damage, working with a hands-on general contractor ensures framing and drywall repairs are handled correctly.
